influences.name: Takeshi Murata
influences.context: I was really, really taken by his still lifes way earlier in the process. There's even a reference to Murata in the liner notes of the record.

influences.name: Brian Reitzell
influences.context: I had a really great friend and mentor in Brian Reitzell who helped me when we would have a challenging bit of a reel where I just got kind of stumped.

influences.name: Tim Hecker
influences.context: I love seeing Tim Hecker perform because the experience truly shakes me.

influences.name: Brian Wilson
influences.context: Although I'm obviously not comparing myself to him, I think of Brian Wilson. His sense of scale was beyond what he understood about what he was doing, beyond what his music could describe. I find something really beautiful in this 'reaching'.

influences.name: Kanye West
influences.context: I've been listening to Kanye West's Yeezus a lot and I think 'Bound 2' is the best track, because the things that are in there are so acute, so precise, that the space around them isn't lost.

influences.name: David Lynch
influences.context: It's like David Lynch's Eraserhead. It's his first movie, he made it with a grant the AFI gave him in 1973. In 1977, he put out this movie, elements of which somehow become embedded in his entire lexicon. Everything is already there and in place, and then we see him improve.

influences.name: Marcel Duchamp
influences.context: It's like Marcel Duchamp and his readymades. He'd take a found object, modify it, reposition it, and it's art. Exactly. This is when my readymade thing starts congealing.

influences.name: Philip K. Dick
influences.context: Do you know how Philip K. Dick did The Man in a High Castle which is an answer to the question, What if the Nazis had won? Well, I wanted to make a movie in my mind of a complete mythos of a band, a town, a kid with a blog, and an alien.

influences.name: Paul Schrader
influences.context: I really have to thank you for that, because it's not something that I think would ever have occurred to me so concretely. [In reference to Schrader's Transcendental Style in Film and concepts of Movement-Image vs Time-Image]

influences.name: Tarkovsky
influences.context: I specifically loved the introduction he wrote for the reissue. He talks about Slow Cinema, non-narrative film, and Tarkovsky. He knows all about that stuff. [Discussed in context of Time-Image manipulation and introspection in cinema]

influences.name: Michael Jackson
influences.context: So, I was like, 'All right, I'm gonna watch Michael Jackson's Super Bowl, I'm gonna watch Prince's Super Bowl, I'm gonna watch everybody.'

influences.name: Prince
influences.context: So, I was like, 'All right, I'm gonna watch Michael Jackson's Super Bowl, I'm gonna watch Prince's Super Bowl, I'm gonna watch everybody.'

influences.name: Simon Reynolds
influences.context: I studied philosophy and read a lot of music writing: Simon Reynolds, music journalism, and essays on the history of contemporary music, electroacoustic music, improvised music, minimalism, and electronic music.

influences.name: Christoph Cox
influences.context: What was the curriculum like? Were you studying with Christoph Cox? Yeah, I did.
